## Summary

This PR fixes an accuracy issue for DeepSeek-V4 when running with PIECEWISE ACLGraph mode on Ascend.

DeepSeek-V4 DSA attention uses the Ascend custom op `vllm::dsa_forward`, but PIECEWISE splitting only added `vllm::mla_forward` as an Ascend custom attention boundary. As a result, the DSA attention path was not treated as a split boundary and could be captured inside a regular PIECEWISE graph segment, leading to incorrect outputs.

This change adds `vllm::dsa_forward` to `compilation_config.splitting_ops` together with `vllm::mla_forward`.

## Changes

- Add `vllm::dsa_forward` to PIECEWISE `splitting_ops`.

## Why

`vllm::dsa_forward` wraps the DeepSeek-V4 DSA attention path. It depends on runtime `forward_context` metadata, KV cache state, sparse attention metadata,and mutates the provided `output` tensor.

Because of these dynamic side effects, it must be handled as a PIECEWISE split boundary instead of being captured inside a normal graph segment.

### What this PR does / why we need it?

Snapshot reusable CPU input metadata with `clone().pin_memory()` before submitting asynchronous H2D transfers in `NPUModelRunner`. This covers `query_start_loc` in input preparation, FIA padding, and dummy runs, plus both direct transfers of `num_computed_tokens` (the speculative `.to()` path and fallback `.copy_()` path).

All production changes are in `vllm_ascend/worker/model_runner_v1.py`. The existing input-preparation event protocol and non-blocking device transfers remain in place. Device buffer addresses, padding contents, and speculative count correction are preserved. The upstream `CpuGpuBuffer` implementation is unchanged.

In the reproduction workload, CPU/device query boundaries disagreed despite the input-preparation event protocol. Snapshotting gives each submitted copy independent source storage. The precise event-ordering gap has not been isolated; this change does not claim that every observed failure was caused by source reuse.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API or configuration changes. The transfers incur additional CPU copies and pinned-memory allocations; their performance impact has not been benchmarked.

### How was this patch tested?

- Ruff lint, Ruff format check, and `git diff --check` passed for the changed files.
- Added `TestQueryStartLocSnapshot.test_padding_transfer_survives_cpu_buffer_reuse` in `tests/ut/worker/test_model_runner_v1.py`. It delays reading the submitted source, overwrites the reusable CPU buffer, and verifies that the padded boundaries remain intact. Updated the existing dummy-run test fixture for the explicit CPU/device transfer.
- On the Ascend reproduction host, ran that exact added test against the extracted production padding method: passed. The method and test were loaded in isolation because the reproduction image has older dependencies than this latest-main PR; the complete test module and full unit suite have not been run.
- Exercised all five production transfer expressions on the host with real torch pinned CPU storage and a simulated delayed transport. All five original-source negative controls observed overwritten values; all five patched expressions retained independent, pinned snapshots. This checks source ownership, not actual DMA timing.
- Earlier end-to-end tests with a broader common-buffer snapshot patch plus the computed-token snapshots completed all 1,319 GSM8K samples. With only the two computed-token snapshots, the workload still failed on D DP2 with `IndexCheck_int64_high_performance_0`; 24 of 1,888 P query-boundary comparisons disagreed. These findings motivated the query-boundary snapshots here; the follow-up validation below still reproduced a failure.
- The repository-wide `format.sh ci` attempt was blocked during markdownlint dependency installation and stopped. No full-suite or CI success is claimed. This PR remains a draft.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/a97dacb7106ee49f39f3d1fc6ae1800ff724e01d

### What this PR does / why we need it?

`InternLM2ForCausalLM` runs on the existing upstream vLLM path, but its checkpoint sets `rope_scaling = {"type": "dynamic", "factor": 2.0}`, which resolves to `DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding`. That class was missing from `REGISTERED_ASCEND_OPS`, so every decoder layer silently fell back to `forward_native` — no log line, no error, just slower.

The same gap affects three other scaled RoPE types. They all share a property: the only thing they change is how the cos/sin cache is computed at init; the forward itself is inherited from `RotaryEmbedding`. So a single mixin (`_AscendScaledRopeMixin`) can route them all to the fused NPU kernel safely:

| `rope_scaling.type` | upstream class | models | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dynamic` + `factor` | `DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding` | InternLM2, InternLM2.5 | `forward_native` | NPU kernel |
| `dynamic` + `alpha` | `DynamicNTKAlphaRotaryEmbedding` | Hunyuan | `forward_native` | NPU kernel |
| `ntk` | `NTKScalingRotaryEmbedding` | — | `forward_native` | NPU kernel |
| `llama3` | `Llama3RotaryEmbedding` | Llama 3.1+ | `forward_native` | NPU kernel |

Three variants are intentionally left out:

- `longrope` / `fope`: they override the forward, not just the cache.
- `linear`: indexes into the cache via the `offsets` arg, which `rope_forward_oot` rejects. Registering it would break multi-LoRA serving.

Dispatch verified on Atlas A2 — each config built through `get_rope`, class printed, excluded types confirmed still on `forward_native`.

**Throughput** (2 × Atlas A2, TP=2, 1024/128, 64 prompts, concurrency 8):

|  | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| req/s | 1.70 | **1.96 (+15.4%)** |
| output tok/s | 216.97 | **250.42** |
| mean TPOT | 33.62 ms | **28.94 ms (−13.9%)** |
| mean TTFT | 435.8 ms | **401.7 ms** |

**Numeric accuracy** (bf16 vs fp32 reference, max abs error on rotated query). The NPU kernel is at least as close as `forward_native` in all cases:

| variant | len | NPU kernel | `forward_native` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| dynamic/factor | 128 | 1.614e-02 | 2.196e-02 |
| dynamic/factor | 2048 | 2.590e-02 | 2.590e-02 |
| dynamic/alpha | 128 | 1.500e-02 | 2.193e-02 |
| dynamic/alpha | 2048 | 2.222e-02 | 3.095e-02 |
| ntk | 128 | 1.548e-02 | 2.041e-02 |
| ntk | 2048 | 1.776e-02 | 3.300e-02 |
| llama3 | 128 | 1.440e-02 | 2.122e-02 |
| llama3 | 2048 | 1.921e-02 | 3.058e-02 |

Also ships the full InternLM2-20B-Chat package: E2E accuracy config, nightly group entry, weight download entry, two-card serving tests, deployment tutorial, and supported-models row.

Closes #10673
Related to #9079

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. Checkpoints with `rope_scaling.type` = `dynamic`, `ntk`, or `llama3` now hit the NPU kernel instead of the reference path. InternLM2-20B-Chat is added to the docs and nightly accuracy suite. Release note fragment included.

### How was this patch tested?

**Environment:** 2 × Atlas A2 (Ascend910_9382, 64 GB), CANN 9.2.1, torch 2.10.0, torch_npu 2.10.0.post7, vLLM `24420b7a`, real BF16 weights (21 shards).

**Unit tests** — 76 passed (`tests/ut/ops/test_rotary_embedding.py`). Parameterized over all four variants: checks that `CustomOp.__new__` resolves to the Ascend class, that the cache comes from the parent, that `use_mtp` is wired up, that every forward arg gets passed through, and that a signature change in the upstream `__init__` will break the build.

**Serving checks** — 13/13 on TP=2 with real weights:

| check | result |
| --- | --- |
| models endpoint | 200 |
| completions, EN + ZH | 200, non-empty |
| greedy reproducible, EN + ZH | token-identical across runs |
| seeded sampling reproducible | identical |
| different seeds diverge | yes |
| 3-turn chat, recall from turn 1 | recalled |
| turn 3 in Chinese | correct |
| retrieval, short prompt (73 tok) | found |
| retrieval, long prompt (5749 tok) | found |

`tests/e2e/pull_request/two_card/test_internlm2_20b_chat.py` encodes these as two pytest cases (one `VllmRunner`, one `RemoteOpenAIServer`) — two model loads total.

**Accuracy** — C-Eval validation (52 subjects, 1346 questions, 5-shot), TP=2, ACL Graph:

```
ceval-valid | acc,none: ground_truth=0.6293 | measured=0.6337 | success=✅
1 passed in 603.84s (0:10:03)
```

Two runs: 0.6293 and 0.6337 (±0.0124 stderr). Baseline set to 0.6293.

**Performance** — numbers in the first section, `vllm bench serve`, same build with/without the registry entries.

**Lint** — `ruff check` + `ruff format --check` clean on the full tree; `codespell` + `markdownlint` clean on new files.

### Checklist

- [x] Four scaled RoPE variants registered and dispatch verified on NPU; three excluded variants confirmed on reference path
- [x] Unit tests for registration, cache inheritance, `use_mtp`, argument forwarding, upstream signature stability
- [x] Two-card E2E tests: offline + online, multi-turn, greedy/sampled, EN/ZH, short/long context
- [x] Accuracy config + nightly group + weight download entry
- [x] Deployment tutorial + supported-models row
- [x] Release note fragment

It is a text-only dense decoder with 48 layers, grouped-query attention (48 query heads over 8 key/value heads, head size 128), SwiGLU feed-forward blocks, RMSNorm, and BF16 weights. The checkpoint declares a 32,768-token context with dynamic NTK RoPE scaling on top of a RoPE theta of 1,000,000. + +This document covers deployment of InternLM2-20B-Chat on Ascend NPUs with vLLM Ascend: weight preparation, service start-up, chat-template behaviour, parallelism choices, and the accuracy and performance figures measured for this tutorial. + +The model architecture `InternLM2ForCausalLM` is implemented upstream in vLLM, so no model definition is added in vLLM Ascend. The dynamic NTK rotary embedding that the checkpoint selects is dispatched to the Ascend fused rotary kernel. + +## 2 Supported Features + +Please refer to the [Supported Models List](../../user_guide/support_matrix/supported_models.md) for the model support matrix, and to the [Feature Guide](../../user_guide/feature_guide/index.md) for feature configuration. + +The following notes are specific to this model: + +| Item | Note | +|------|------| +| Weight format | BF16 only; no quantized checkpoint is published upstream | +| Context length | 32,768 tokens, from `max_position_embeddings` | +| RoPE | `rope_scaling.type=dynamic` with `factor=2.0`; see section 9.1 | +| Expert parallelism | Not applicable, the model is dense | +| Multimodal input | Not applicable, the model is text-only | +| Speculative decoding (MTP) | Not available, the checkpoint ships no draft weights | + +## 3 Prerequisites + +### 3.1 Model Weight + +| Model | Weight size | Hardware requirement | Download | +|-------|------------:|----------------------|----------| +| InternLM2-20B-Chat | about 37 GiB in 21 safetensors shards | 2 Atlas A2 inference products (64GB) | [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/Shanghai_AI_Laboratory/internlm2-chat-20b), [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/internlm/internlm2-chat-20b) | + +The weights alone exceed half of a single 64 GB device, so tensor parallelism of 2 is the recommended baseline: it leaves room for the KV cache, the graph capture buffers, and the activation peak. The accuracy workflow in this repository sets `VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True`, so the end-to-end configuration refers to the ModelScope namespace `Shanghai_AI_Laboratory/internlm2-chat-20b`. + +Download the weights to a directory of your choice and record it: + +```bash +pip install modelscope +modelscope download \ + --model Shanghai_AI_Laboratory/internlm2-chat-20b \ + --local_dir your_model_path [Installation Guide](../../getting_started/installation.md). + +To verify the installation: + +```bash +pip show vllm-ascend +``` + +Expected result: the version information is displayed. + +## 5 Online Service Deployment {: #5-online-service-deployment } + +### 5.1 Starting the Server + +> The following command is an example configuration. Adjust the parameters based on your actual scenario. + +=== "Atlas A2 inference products / Atlas A3 inference products" + + ```bash + export ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 + export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True + # Ensure the model path matches the directory recorded during download + vllm serve your_model_path \ + --served-model-name internlm2-20b-chat \ + --trust-remote-code \ + --tensor-parallel-size 2 \ + --dtype bfloat16 \ + --max-model-len 4096 \ + --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \ + --port + ``` + +### 5.2 Parameter Description + +| Parameter | Note | +|-----------|------| +| `--trust-remote-code` | Required. The repository ships `configuration_internlm2.py` and `tokenization_internlm2.py` through `auto_map`, and the tokenizer cannot be built without them. The model itself still runs the native vLLM implementation, not the remote `modeling_internlm2.py`. | +| `--tensor-parallel-size` | 2 is the recommended baseline on 64 GB devices. Both 48 query heads and 8 key/value heads divide by 2 and by 4, so TP=4 is also valid; see section 9.2 for the trade-off. | +| `--dtype bfloat16` | Matches the published checkpoint. | +| `--max-model-len` | Up to 32768. Raising it increases the per-sequence KV cache, so reduce `--max-num-seqs` accordingly. | + +### 5.3 Chat Template + +The checkpoint ships a ChatML chat template, so `/v1/chat/completions` works without passing `--chat-template`. Each turn is wrapped as: + +```text +<|im_start|>{role} +{content}<|im_end|> +``` + +Two properties are worth noting: + +- The template emits `bos_token` once at the start of the conversation, not per turn. +- The assistant turn ends with `<|im_end|>` (id 92542). `generation_config.json` lists `eos_token_id: [2, 92542]`, so both `` and `<|im_end|>` terminate generation. Keep `generation_config.json` next to the weights; without it, only `` is treated as a stop token and completions run on past the end of the turn. + +The system role is supported. If no system message is supplied, the template simply omits it. + +### 5.4 Service Verification + +The service is ready once the model list is returned: + +```bash +curl http://localhost:/v1/models +``` + +Expected result: HTTP 200 with `internlm2-20b-chat` in the `data` list. + +## 6 Functional Verification + +**Chat Completions API:** + +```bash +curl http://localhost:/v1/chat/completions \ + -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ + -d '{ + "model": "internlm2-20b-chat", + "messages": [ + {"role": "user", "content": "Give me a short introduction to large language models."} + ], + "temperature": 0, + "max_tokens": 128 + }' +``` + +Expected result: HTTP 200 with a JSON response whose `choices[0].message.content` is non-empty and whose `finish_reason` is `stop` or `length`. + +**Completions API:** + +```bash +curl http://localhost:/v1/completions \ + -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ + -d '{ + "model": "internlm2-20b-chat", + "prompt": "Shanghai is", + "temperature": 0, + "max_tokens": 32 + }' +``` + +**Multi-turn chat:** pass the previous assistant reply back in `messages`. The response must stay on topic and must not contain the literal markers `<|im_start|>` or `<|im_end|>`; their appearance in the output means the stop tokens were not applied. + +## 7 Accuracy Evaluation + +This repository ships an end-to-end configuration at `tests/e2e/models/configs/InternLM2-20B-Chat.yaml`, evaluated with lm-eval on the C-Eval validation split. + +```bash +export VLLM_USE_MODELSCOPE=True + +pytest -sv tests/e2e/models/test_lm_eval_correctness.py \ + --config tests/e2e/models/configs/InternLM2-20B-Chat.yaml \ + --report-dir ./benchmarks/accuracy +``` + +The configuration pins the parallelism, so no `--tp-size` is required. The test compares the measured metric against the checked-in baseline with the repository-wide relative tolerance and writes a Markdown report to the report directory. + +| Dataset | Shots | Metric | Value | +|---------|------:|--------|------:| +| ceval-valid | 5 | acc,none | 0.6293 | + +## 8 Performance Evaluation + +Refer to the [vLLM benchmark](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/benchmarking/) documentation for details. Take `serve` as an example, against a running server: + +```shell +vllm bench serve \ + --model your_model_path \ + --served-model-name internlm2-20b-chat \ + --port \ + --dataset-name random \ + --random-input-len 1024 \ + --random-output-len 128 \ + --num-prompts 64 \ + --max-concurrency 8 \ + --ignore-eos +``` + +Keep input length, output length, request count, and concurrency fixed when comparing configurations; results obtained under different settings are not comparable. + +The command above, run against a TP=2 server started with `--max-model-len 8192 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.85` on two Atlas A2 devices, gives: + +| TP | Max model len | Requests | Concurrency | Request throughput | Output throughput | Mean TTFT | Mean TPOT | +|---:|--------------:|---------:|------------:|-------------------:|------------------:|----------:|----------:| +| 2 | 8192 | 64 | 8 | 1.96 req/s | 250.42 tok/s | 401.7 ms | 28.9 ms | + +## 9 Performance Tuning + +Please refer to the [vLLM Features](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/stable/features), [vLLM Ascend Additional Configuration](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/user_guide/configuration/additional_config.html) and [vLLM Ascend Feature Guide](https://docs.vllm.ai/projects/ascend/en/latest/user_guide/feature_guide) for key parameter descriptions. + +### 9.1 Dynamic NTK RoPE + +The checkpoint declares `rope_scaling = {"type": "dynamic", "factor": 2.0}`. vLLM builds a `DynamicNTKScalingRotaryEmbedding` for it. Because the checkpoint provides no `max_trained_positions`, vLLM defaults it to `max_position_embeddings`, the NTK correction term collapses to one, and the resulting cos/sin table is identical to a plain RoPE table at theta 1,000,000. Serving at the full 32,768-token context therefore needs no additional scaling configuration. + +This rotary variant is dispatched to the Ascend fused rotary kernel. On releases where that dispatch is absent, the layer silently falls back to the elementwise reference implementation; nothing in the log reports the fallback, so confirm the class in use when debugging rotary behaviour on this model. Measured on two Atlas A2 devices with the workload above, the fused kernel was worth 15.4% in output throughput and 13.9% in mean time per output token, and its bf16 output was closer to an fp32 reference than the fallback at every sequence length tested. + +### 9.2 Parallelism + +The attention shape divides evenly at both TP=2 and TP=4. Higher tensor parallelism lowers the per-device weight and KV-cache footprint, but the upstream InternLM2 implementation stores q, k, and v interleaved in a single `wqkv` projection and reconstructs them with an all-gather in every decoder layer, so collective traffic grows with the degree of tensor parallelism. On 64 GB devices, TP=2 is the recommended starting point; move to TP=4 only when the memory headroom at the target context length and batch size requires it. + +### 9.3 General Tuning Reference + +Please refer to the [Public Performance Tuning Documentation](../../developer_guide/performance_and_debug/optimization_and_tuning.md) for tuning methods, and to the [Feature Matrix](../../user_guide/support_matrix/feature_matrix.md) for feature descriptions. + +## 10 FAQ + +For common environment, installation, and general parameter issues, please refer to the [Public FAQs](../../faqs.md). This section only covers issues specific to InternLM2-20B-Chat. + +### 10.1 The tokenizer fails to load + +The error names `tokenization_internlm2` or `InternLM2Tokenizer`. Pass `--trust-remote-code` and make sure the Python files from the model repository were downloaded alongside the weights. + +### 10.2 Generation does not stop at the end of a turn + +The reply continues past the answer or contains `<|im_start|>`. Check that `generation_config.json` is present in the model directory: it carries `eos_token_id: [2, 92542]`, and `tokenizer_config.json` alone declares only ``. + +### 10.3 Out of memory at start-up or during graph capture + +Confirm that `--tensor-parallel-size` is at least 2, then lower `--max-num-seqs`, `--max-model-len`, or `--gpu-memory-utilization`.
